subject: ventures/1099k-reconciliation-worksheet
professional: an enrolled agent or CPA who prepares returns for marketplace sellers and reconciles Form 1099-K box 1a to Schedule C gross receipts. First checks: is box 1a treated as gross (not net of fees, refunds, chargebacks), does the worksheet keep line 1 tied to the 1099-K total with returns on line 2 so IRS document matching (CP2000) does not fire, are personal items sold at a loss, reimbursements, gifts and forms received in error kept off Schedule C (Schedule 1 lines 8z/24z), are costs mapped to Schedule C lines, and are any reporting thresholds it states current after the One Big Beautiful Bill Act restored $20,000 and 200 transactions

evidence.correctness: Recomputed with node -e against calc.mjs. (1) Own row box1a 23456.78, refunds 1234.56, sales tax 987.65, fees 2345.67, COGS 8765.43, shipping 1111.11: by hand (Schedule C order: line 1 minus line 2, minus COGS and expenses) adjustments 2222.21, receipts 21234.57, costs 12222.21, net 9012.36; tool identical. (2) 200 rows of box1a 0.10 with refund 0.01: Decimal by hand 20.00 / 2.00 / 18.00; tool identical, no float drift. (3) Boundary of the disclosed 15% share: 150/1000 no finding, 150.01/1000 fires. Arithmetic is right. Wrong in a common case: a Poshmark row of box1a 3000 with 'cost of goods' 8000 (used personal clothing sold below what it cost) gives estimated net profit -5000.00 and a finding saying 'A loss is common when building inventory or clearing stock below cost -- keep the receipts that support it'. Per the Instructions for Schedule 1 (Form 1040), lines 8z and 24z, and the IRS 'Understanding your Form 1099-K' guidance, personal items sold at a loss are reported on Schedule 1 8z and offset on 24z, net zero, and the loss is not deductible; carrying -5000 to Schedule C would offset wage income. The tool names Poshmark, Mercari and Depop, mostly closet sellers, as its audience. Also, with one clamped row (A: 100 box1a, 130 refunds; B: 1000) the CSV TOTAL line reads box1a 1100, adjustments 130, adjusted receipts 1000, which does not foot (1100 - 130 = 970).
evidence.completeness: node --test '*.test.mjs': 48 pass. Claimed features checked end to end in node: reconcileRow (refunds and marketplace-remitted sales tax backed out, then fees/COGS/shipping), high finding when adjustments exceed box 1a (fires, floors at 0), medium finding over 15% (fires at 150.01/1000), info loss finding (fires), reconcileAll totals and always-on not-a-filing finding (present), toCsv with TOTAL line only for more than one row (works), share link capped at 25 rows with per-field coercion (share.mjs:26,61), usage counting local with DNT/GPC and opt-out (usage.mjs, usage.test.mjs). Explainer and comparison pages exist and are linked and in the sitemap. node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin (live host 403 through the proxy). No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 48 tests, 0 fail, 0.14 s. Seven mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py (one more, rewriting the net-profit total as an equivalent expression, survived but is equivalent and is not counted). Caught 4: 15% '>' -> '>=', shipping dropped from costs, loss finding threshold moved to -100, negatives no longer floored. Survived 3: combined totalExpenses replaced by the last row's costs (calc.mjs:110), combined adjusted receipts summing the unclamped raw figure (calc.mjs:109), and CSV fees/COGS columns swapped under their headers (calc.mjs:167). No test asserts totals.totalExpenses or any CSV cell value, so the combined Costs column and the exported file a preparer receives are unguarded.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (185 lines), calc.test.mjs, share.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html, page.test.mjs. Small pure module, round2 per step, CSV quoting, HTML escaping of the platform name, share decoder that coerces every field and caps rows. Weaknesses: nonNegNumber silently turns '1,200' or '-50' into 0 (calc.mjs:28-32; the form uses type=number, which limits this to share links and stored rows); clamping adjusted receipts at 0 per row makes the TOTAL line not foot; the README dev command 'node --test' is the form Node 22 rejects in this repo's guidance.
evidence.claims: Backed: box 1a gross 'without regard to any adjustments for credits, cash equivalents, discounts, fees, refunds' matches the General Instructions for Forms 1099-K; disclaimer (index.html:137 and both sub-pages), nothing uploaded (no fetch in the page; page.test.mjs:37), local usage counting with DNT/GPC and an opt-out button (index.html:140, usage.mjs). No reporting threshold is stated on this page; the linked 1099-k-threshold-checker encodes the OBBBA restoration of $20,000/200 retroactive to 2022 (its calc.mjs:13-25), and the 1099-NEC tracker link's '2026 $2,000' matches OBBBA. Not backed: index.html:127 FAQ answers 'Do I have to report the full Box 1a amount as income?' with 'No' and tells the user to report gross receipts 'after backing out' refunds; the Schedule C instructions have the 1099-K amounts included in line 1 gross receipts with returns and allowances on line 2, so the IRS can match the form. index.html:107 attributes the inclusion of marketplace-remitted sales tax to 'the IRS's own General Instructions for Forms 1099-K', which say nothing about sales tax; calc.mjs:13 correctly attributes it to processors' own guidance. README.md:6 and VENTURE.yaml call the result 'estimated net taxable profit' though it ignores every Schedule C expense other than fees, COGS and shipping.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through as an EA: two marketplace 1099-Ks, one reseller (Etsy) and one closet seller (Poshmark). The Etsy row reconciles and exports; but the CSV has no Schedule C line mapping (line 1 gross, line 2 returns, Part III COGS with opening/closing inventory, line 10 commissions and fees, shipping as supplies/other or in COGS), so the preparer re-keys it. The Poshmark row cannot be expressed correctly: no 'personal items' flag routes it to Schedule 1 8z/24z or to Form 8949 for a gain; no row type for Venmo/PayPal reimbursements, gifts, or a 1099-K received in error (also Schedule 1 8z/24z). A seller on a payment app gets every friends-and-family payment treated as gross receipts.
evidence.domain: Compared with the General Instructions for Forms 1099-K (box 1a gross), the Instructions for Schedule C (line 1 includes 1099-K amounts, line 2 returns and allowances, Part III COGS), the Instructions for Schedule 1 (Form 1040) lines 8z/24z for personal items sold at a loss and forms received in error, and Pub 334 on sales tax collected by a seller. Matches: gross treatment of box 1a, fees and refunds as reconciling items, marketplace-facilitator tax not seller income. Departs: nets refunds and sales tax out of 'gross receipts' instead of keeping line 1 tied to the forms; treats every row as a business with deductible losses; no personal-item, reimbursement, gift or error treatment; no hint that box 1a may need to be checked against the monthly boxes 5a-5l or that multiple forms can cover the same receipts. A preparer would use it as scratch arithmetic, not sign off on it as a reconciliation.

defects.what: Every row is treated as a business: personal items sold below cost (the typical Poshmark, Mercari, Depop seller the page targets) produce a negative 'estimated net profit' and a finding encouraging the user to keep receipts for the loss. Per the Schedule 1 (Form 1040) instructions, lines 8z/24z, such a loss is reported and offset to zero and is not deductible; a -5000 carried to Schedule C would offset wages.

FAQ answers 'No' to reporting the full box 1a and tells users to report receipts already net of refunds and sales tax; the Schedule C instructions put 1099-K amounts in line 1 and returns in line 2, and a line 1 below the 1099-K total invites an IRS matching notice.

No row type for payment-app reimbursements, gifts, or a 1099-K received in error (Schedule 1 8z/24z), and no personal-item gain route to Form 8949; the README invites 'any other ... payment app' users.
3 of 7 non-equivalent mutants survive: combined totalExpenses, combined adjusted receipts and CSV column order are untested, so the combined Costs column and the preparer's CSV are unguarded.
CSV has no Schedule C line mapping (line 1, line 2, Part III COGS, line 10 fees, shipping), so a preparer must re-key every figure.

Page attributes the inclusion of marketplace-remitted sales tax in box 1a to the IRS General Instructions for Forms 1099-K, which do not mention sales tax (calc.mjs:13 correctly credits platform guidance).
Per-row clamp of adjusted receipts at 0 makes the TOTAL line not foot (1100 - 130 shown as 1000).
README and VENTURE.yaml call the output 'estimated net taxable profit' though it ignores every Schedule C expense except fees, COGS and shipping.
nonNegNumber silently maps '1,200' and negatives to 0 for share-link and stored rows.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: an independent row with cents in every field, a 200-row exact-decimal sum and the 15% boundary all recompute exactly, the disclaimer and local usage counting with an opt-out are present, and no reporting threshold on or linked from the page is stale after OBBBA. It misses the bar on correctness, verification and claims. It models every 1099-K row as a business, so a closet seller's personal items sold below cost come out as a deductible $5,000 loss with a finding that encourages keeping receipts for it, where the Schedule 1 8z/24z rule nets to zero. Its FAQ tells users not to report the full box 1a, against the Schedule C line 1/line 2 layout that keeps the return tied to the form. 3 of 7 mutants survive, including the combined Costs total and the CSV column order. An EA would use it as scratch arithmetic, not as a reconciliation they sign.
